sectionBlueprint.heading: Why The Grail Keeps Changing Shape

qa.question: Was the Grail always a cup?
qa.answer: No. Early versions do not always present it as the Last Supper cup; that identification developed strongly through later Christianized tradition.

qa.question: Who first popularized the Grail in Arthurian romance?
qa.answer: Chretien de Troyes popularized the grail in Perceval, though his work was unfinished.

qa.question: Who made the Grail Christ's cup?
qa.answer: Robert de Boron was central in connecting the Grail to Joseph of Arimathea and Christ's cup.

qa.question: Who completes the Grail Quest?
qa.answer: In later Christianized Arthurian tradition, Galahad completes the quest because of his purity.

qa.question: Has the Holy Grail been found?
qa.answer: No verified object can be identified as the legendary Holy Grail.
